sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014. The Shakara [=Tari] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout February 28, 2014). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. the Internet Archive 20150421041126 of rogerblench.info.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 3: 'The tone system of Shakara has only two tones and the majority of words appear all low tone. A few possible cases of glide tones occur.' Sister lect (Shakara), not Nyeng itself.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request Number 2008-017 (submitted by K. Hannelova, M. Rueck, Z. Yoder, C. Magnusson, SIL Nigeria Group, dated 2007-10-31): merge [nfg] Nyeng and [nfk] Shakara into [nfd], rename Ahwai. SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; only that speakers say the three varieties are one language 'with different intonation', >86% lexical similarity on 320-item wordlists, similar noun-class marking.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Ndun language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout September 4, 2007). 27 pp. the Internet Archive 20150421041121 of rogerblench.info. wordlist
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3.3 Tones pp. 2-3: two tones (H, L) plus rising/falling; 'a significant number of words.. seem to have a mid-tone on the last syllable, following a high-low sequence. This appears to be conditioned'; tone plurals common. Sister lect (Ndun), not Nyeng itself.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Nyeng language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment (printout January 4, 2006). Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 24 pp. [data: Adu village, 22 June 2003]. Retrieved from the Internet Archive 20150421041124 of rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Plateau/Ndunic/Nyeng wordlist
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (printed pp. 2-3; 'based on rapid observations.. tentative'): seven (perhaps only five) vowels, consonant chart, sec. 3.3 Tones: 'Nyeng appears to have two tones, high and low.. also rising and falling tones'. The word 'stress'/'accent' does not occur in the document.
